prompt: A vertical 9:16 close-up photograph of a British woman in her early eighties standing just inside her front door at dusk, looking down at a glossy A5 flyer held in both hands, its back to the camera so only her face and the top edge of the paper fill the frame. She wears a buttoned navy wool winter coat and a grey knitted bobble hat indoors, a pair of reading glasses low on her nose. Her face is soft with pity, brows slightly raised, mouth just parting as if about to speak, not a pout, not a smile. Her skin is thin and lined, with liver spots on her cheek and a few loose strands of uneven white hair escaping the hat. The only light is a cold, flat grey-blue from the frosted glass panel of the door on the left, with a faint warm orange spill from a hallway bulb behind her on the right; blacks are lifted and contrast is low. The camera is at her chest height looking slightly up, framed off-centre so her face sits in the upper third and the hat is cut by the top edge. Shot on a cheap consumer digital camera in low light, soft, slightly smeared, with visible noise and no crisp detail. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph of a narrow council-flat hallway at dusk, seen at eye level from the doorway of the front room, the painted door frame cutting into the left side of the picture. An elderly working-class British woman, about eighty, in a long brown winter coat, a burgundy knitted hat and fleece slippers, stands on a worn patterned doormat by the front door. A small pile of junk mail lies at her feet. She holds one flyer out at arm's length to read it, its face towards the camera: a sad, well-fed middle-aged man in an expensive coat above the words "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" in bold white sans-serif on red. She tilts her head with a look of genuine sympathy. The walls are magnolia woodchip, a draught excluder lies along the bottom of the door, and a coat hook is crowded with scarves and a shopping bag. The light is a single weak bare bulb overhead, warm and dim, against cold blue dusk through the reeded glass of the front door. Colour negative film with fine grain, low contrast, a normal lens, slightly high camera, nothing tidy. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from across the street at late blue hour, looking at the lower corner of a three-storey brown-brick council block under a flat overcast sky. The light is very low and even, with no shadows, the brick a cold slate grey shading to maroon, the blacks lifted and soft as if through drizzle. Only one ground-floor window is lit: behind a white uPVC frame with a violet-blue edge from the sky, cream vertical blinds are half open and a bare ceiling bulb glows warm amber. Through the gap, small in the frame, an elderly woman in a winter coat and knitted hat sits forward in an armchair, holding a sheet of paper close to her face and looking at it, the cold blue flicker of an old television on the far wall. The upper windows are dark. The camera is on a tripod at eye level, a normal-to-slightly-long lens, verticals straight, the building filling most of the frame with a sliver of grey sky at the top and the lit window placed low and off-centre. A long exposure with soft, smudged detail, quiet and lonely, in the manner of Todd Hido's night houses. Thanks.
